content.title: About
content.content: Spaghetti sauce with added vegetables is a ready‑to‑use tomato sauce enriched with carrots, celery, bell pepper and onion. It is designed for quick pasta preparation, giving the dish a rich flavor and an extra serving of vegetables.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The sauce typically contains tomatoes, carrots, celery, onion and bell pepper, making it more nutritious than plain tomato sauce.
The vegetables are heat‑treated, preserving most of their vitamins and antioxidants.
It is popular in diet plans because it adds vegetables without the need to cook them separately.
Some versions include basil or oregano to boost aromatic notes.
The product can be ready‑to‑eat or require a brief heating before serving.

items.title: Rich in lycopene
items.content: Tomatoes provide lycopene, a powerful antioxidant that supports heart health and skin.

items.title: Source of vitamin A
items.content: Carrots and bell pepper supply beta‑carotene, which the body converts to vitamin A.

items.title: Contains vitamin C
items.content: Tomatoes and pepper are good sources of vitamin C, aiding immune function.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Fiber from the vegetables helps maintain healthy gastrointestinal function.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Unlike creamy sauces, this product contains minimal fat, making it suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Some versions can be high in salt; people monitoring sodium intake should check the label.

items.title: Tomato allergy
items.content: A small number of individuals may experience allergic reactions to tomatoes or other ingredients.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: Industrial production may use preservatives; choose additive‑free options if preferred.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: A modest amount of sugar is sometimes added for balance; diabetics should take this into account.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heat the sauce in a saucepan or microwave, add it to cooked spaghetti and stir. It can also be used in lasagna, casseroles, as a pizza base, or as a dip for vegetable sticks.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the unopened sauce in a cool, dry place. After opening, keep it refrigerated and consume within 5‑7 days. Discard if it develops an off‑odor or discoloration.
